module option for Option<T>

The ways out of an Option<T>, in the prelude, each stating what absence gives. There is no unwrap. map and filter over an option are the core's steps applied to the present value. See Option: a value that may be missing.

  • is_some — Whether self holds a value: some(3) | is_some is true.
  • is_none — Whether self is none: [1, 2][5] | is_none is true.
  • unwrap_or — The value of self when present, and default otherwise: [1, 2][5] | unwrap_or(0) is 0.
  • unwrap_or_else — The value of self when present, and what default returns otherwise; default is called only when self is none: [1, 2][5] | unwrap_or_else(() => 7) is 7.
  • and_then — by applied to the value of self when present, its own none kept, and none otherwise: [4][0] | and_then(x => [10][x]) is none.
  • or_else — self when present, and the option default returns otherwise: [1][5] | or_else(() => [9][0]) is 9.
  • alternative — self when present, and other otherwise: [1][5] | alternative([9][0]) is 9.

docs.text:
module regex

Text matched against a regular expression. A pattern is a String; one that does not parse is an evaluation error at the call. The module is imported where it is used: import regex.

  • is_match — Whether pattern matches somewhere in text: "a1b22c" | regex.is_match("[0-9]+") is true.
  • find — The first match of pattern in text, or none: "a1b22c" | regex.find("[0-9]+") is "1".
  • find_all — Every non-overlapping match of pattern in text, in order: "a1b22c" | regex.find_all("[0-9]+") is ["1", "22"].
  • captures — The first match of pattern in text and its groups, whole match first, or none; a group that took no part in the match is "": "a" | regex.captures("(a)|(b)") is ["a", "a", ""].
  • replace_all — text with every match of pattern replaced by replacement, in which $1 is the first group: "a1b22c" | regex.replace_all("([0-9]+)", "<$1>") is "a<1>b<22>c".
  • replace_first — text with the first match of pattern replaced by replacement, in which $1 is the first group: "a1b22c" | regex.replace_first("[0-9]+", "#") is "a#b22c".
  • split — The pieces of text between matches of pattern, in order: "a1b22c" | regex.split("[0-9]+") is ["a", "b", "c"].

module result for Result<T, E>

The ways out of a Result<T, E>, in the prelude, each stating what a failure gives. A result is ok(v) or err(e). There is no unwrap. map over a result is the core's step applied to the value of a success: ok(3) | map(n => n + 1) is ok(4).

  • is_ok — Whether self is a success: ok(4) | is_ok is true.
  • is_err — Whether self is a failure: err("x") | is_err is true.
  • ok — The value of self when a success, and none when a failure: err("x") | ok is none.
  • err — The error of self when a failure, and none when a success: ok(4) | err is none.
  • unwrap_or — The value of self when a success, and default when a failure: err("x") | unwrap_or(0) is 0.
  • unwrap_or_else — The value of self when a success, and default applied to the error when a failure: err("ab") | unwrap_or_else(e => e.size()) is 2.
  • map_err — A failure with by applied to its error; a success is kept as it is: err("x") | map_err(e => e.upper()) is err("X").
  • and_then — by applied to the value of a success, its own failure kept; a failure is kept as it is: ok(4) | and_then(n => ok(n * 2)) is ok(8).
  • or_else — by applied to the error of a failure, giving another result; a success is kept as it is: err("x") | or_else(e => ok(e.size())) is ok(1).

  • Ranking — The hits of one retrieval, as a Seq<Hit<T>> in descending order of score, ties ordered by name, with the query they are relative to and the retrieval that produced them.

docs.title: std/seq
docs.text:
module seq for Seq<T>

The sequence, set and map operations beyond the core's membership, order and lookup, in the prelude. A receiver module over Seq<T>, with T bound per call; a function that takes any collection writes its receiver, self: Collection<T>, and the functions over sets and maps take theirs as a typed first parameter. A receiver S : Seq<T> comes back at its own type, and F<_> : Seq<_> rebuilt in its own constructor.

  • first — The element at position 0, or none over an empty sequence: [3, 1, 2] | first is 3.
  • last — The element at the last position, or none over an empty sequence: [3, 1, 2] | last is 2.
  • reverse — The elements of self in the opposite order, in its own constructor: [1, 2, 3] | reverse is [3, 2, 1].
  • distinct — Each value of self once, at its first position, at the type of self: [1, 2, 1, 3, 2] | distinct is [1, 2, 3].
  • zip — Pairs of the elements of self and other at equal positions, as long as the shorter: [1, 2, 3] | zip(["a", "b"]) is [Pair(first = 1, second = "a"), Pair(first = 2, second = "b")].
  • enumerate — Each element of self paired with its position, counting from 0: ["a", "b"] | enumerate is [Pair(first = 0, second = "a"), Pair(first = 1, second = "b")].
  • any — Whether by holds of some value of self; false over an empty collection: [1, 2, 3] | any(x => x > 2) is true.
  • all — Whether by holds of every value of self; true over an empty collection: [] | all(x => x > 2) is true.
  • find — The first element of self that by accepts, or none: [1, 2, 3, 4] | find(x => x > 2) is 3.
  • position — The position of the first element of self that by accepts, counting from 0, or none: [1, 2, 3, 4] | position(x => x > 2) is 2.
  • take_while — The leading values of self that by accepts, up to the first it rejects: [1, 2, 5, 1] | take_while(x => x < 3) is [1, 2].
  • drop_while — The values of self after the leading ones by accepts, at the type of self: [1, 2, 5, 1] | drop_while(x => x < 3) is [5, 1].
  • window — Every run of n consecutive elements of self, in order: [1, 2, 3, 4] | window(2) is [[1, 2], [2, 3], [3, 4]].
  • partition — The values of self redistributed by the key by gives: each value once, at its own type, those of one key in one logical partition.
  • is_empty — Whether self has no values: [] | is_empty is true.
  • join — Every pair of a value of self and a value of other that by relates, in the order of self, then of other: [1, 2] | join([1, 2, 3], (a, b) => a < b) gives the pairs (1, 2), (1, 3) and (2, 3).
  • min_by — The value of self that is least, by the key by gives or by the Ordering by gives two values; the first of equals, or none over an empty collection: ["bb", "a", "ccc"] | min_by(s => size(s)) is "a".
  • max_by — The value of self that is greatest, by the key by gives or by the Ordering by gives two values; the first of equals, or none over an empty collection: ["bb", "a", "ccc"] | max_by(s => size(s)) is "ccc".
  • to_map — A map from the key of each value of self to its value; two values with one key are an evaluation error: ["bb", "a"] | to_map(s => s, s => size(s)) is Map {"bb": 2, "a": 1}.
  • range — The Ints from start up to, not including, end, each step after the one before: range(1, 6) is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], and range(10, 0, -3) is [10, 7, 4, 1].
  • with — The map self with key set to value, added or replaced, at the type of self: Map(["a"], [1]) | with("b", 2) is Map {"a": 1, "b": 2}.
  • without — The map self without key, whether or not it held it, at the type of self: Map(["a", "b"], [1, 2]) | without("a") is Map {"b": 2}.
  • entries — Each association of the map self as a Pair of its key and its value, in the map's order.
  • values — The values of the map self, in the map's order: Map(["b", "a"], [2, 1]) | values is [2, 1].
  • intersection — The members of both self and other, at the type of self: {1, 2, 3} | intersection({2, 3, 4}) is {2, 3}.
  • difference — The members of self that other does not hold, at the type of self: {1, 2, 3} | difference({2, 3, 4}) is {1}.

docs.title: std/string
docs.text:
module string for String

The functions of a String, in the prelude. A receiver module: each function takes self, so s.trim(), string.trim(s) and s | trim are one declaration. A String is a sequence of Unicode scalar values held as UTF-8, whatever encoding its text was read from. Positions and size count code points.

  • str — The text self prints as, for a value of any type: str(some(2)) is "2".
  • fmt — The template self with each {} replaced by the text of the next of args, in order: fmt("{} of {}", 1, some(2)) is "1 of 2".
  • length — How many characters self has, counting code points: "héllo" | length is 5.
  • size — How many characters self has, counting code points; the same as length: "héllo" | size is 5.
  • upper — self in upper case: "Straße" | upper is "STRASSE".
  • lower — self in lower case: "ÀB" | lower is "àb".
  • trim — self without leading and trailing whitespace: " a b " | trim is "a b".
  • trim_start — self without leading whitespace: " a " | trim_start is "a ".
  • trim_end — self without trailing whitespace: " a " | trim_end is " a".
  • capitalize — self with its first character in upper case: "élan" | capitalize is "Élan".
  • split — The pieces of self between occurrences of separator, in order: "a,b,,c" | split(",") is ["a", "b", "", "c"].
  • join — The texts of self in order, with separator between each two: ["a", "b"].join(", ") is "a, b".
  • replace_all — self with every occurrence of from replaced by to: "aaa" | replace_all("a", "b") is "bbb".
  • replace_first — self with the first occurrence of from replaced by to: "aaa" | replace_first("a", "b") is "baa".
  • starts_with — Whether self begins with part: "hello" | starts_with("he") is true.
  • ends_with — Whether self ends with part: "hello" | ends_with("lo") is true.
  • contains — Whether part occurs in self: "hello" | contains("ell") is true.
  • index_of — The position of the first occurrence of part in self, counting characters from 0, or none: "héllo" | index_of("l") is 2.
  • last_index_of — The position of the last occurrence of part in self, counting characters from 0, or none: "héllo" | last_index_of("l") is 3.
  • occurrences — How many non-overlapping times part occurs in self; 0 for an empty part: "aaaa" | occurrences("aa") is 2.
  • strip_prefix — self without part at its start, or none when it does not begin with it: "x.hql" | strip_prefix("x.") is "hql".
  • strip_suffix — self without part at its end, or none when it does not end with it: "x.hql" | strip_suffix(".hql") is "x".
  • trim_prefix — self without part at its start, or self as it is when it does not begin with it: "x" | trim_prefix("y") is "x".
  • trim_suffix — self without part at its end, or self as it is when it does not end with it: "x.hql" | trim_suffix(".hql") is "x".
  • equals_ignore_case — Whether self and other are equal in lower case: "ABC" | equals_ignore_case("abc") is true.
  • chars — Each character of self as its own text, in order: "héy" | chars is ["h", "é", "y"].
  • lines — The lines of self, without their line breaks; a final line break opens no empty line: string.lines("a\nb\n") is ["a", "b"].
  • words — The whitespace-separated words of self: " a b\tc " | words is ["a", "b", "c"].
  • reverse — The characters of self in the opposite order: "héllo" | reverse is "olléh".
  • repeat — self written times times in a row; "" for times below 1: "ab" | repeat(3) is "ababab".
  • pad_left — self preceded by fill, repeated, until it is width characters long; a longer self as it is: "7" | pad_left(3, "0") is "007".
  • pad_right — self followed by fill, repeated, until it is width characters long; a longer self as it is: "7" | pad_right(3, "0") is "700".
  • center — self between fills until it is width characters long; an odd fill character goes after it: "ab" | center(5, "*") is "*ab**".
  • truncate — At most the first width characters of self: "hello" | truncate(3) is "hel".
  • slice — The characters of self from start up to, not including, end, counting from 0; s[start:end].
  • char_at — The character of self at position, counting from 0, or none outside the text: "hello" | char_at(1) is "e".
  • to_int — The integer self writes, surrounding whitespace aside, or none when it writes none: "-42" | to_int is -42, and "1.5" | to_int is none.
  • to_float — The number self writes, as a Float, or none when it writes none: "1e3" | to_float is 1000.0.
  • to_decimal — The exact decimal number self writes, at its written scale, or none when it writes none: "2.50" | to_decimal is 2.50.
  • to_bool — The truth value self writes as true or false, or none for any other text: "True" | to_bool is none.
  • is_empty — Whether self has no characters: "" | is_empty is true.
  • is_blank — Whether self has no characters other than whitespace: " " | is_blank is true.
  • ord — The Unicode code point of the one-character text self, or none for any other text: "a" | ord is 97.
  • chr — The one-character text of the Unicode code point self, or none for an Int that is none: 97 | chr is "a".
  • bytes — The UTF-8 encoding of self, one Int per byte: "é" | bytes is [195, 169].

docs.title: std/validators
docs.text:
module validators

Validators: the standard validator types, imported where they are used, import validators, and never by the prelude, so a program's own Email is its own. A field declared with one, email: Email, is of the one type that implements it; NonEmpty, implemented for more than one type, is named in a rule, validate tags with NonEmpty, where the field's type selects the implementation. A broken one is the violation Contract.f of kind rule.

  • Email — An email address: one @ with text before it, and a domain after it holding a . that neither opens nor closes it.
  • NonEmpty — Text that is more than whitespace, or a list with an element.

docs.title: Implementations
docs.text:
impl Email for String

A String is an Email when it holds exactly one @, does not open with it, and the text after it contains a . and neither opens nor closes with one.

impl NonEmpty for String

A String is NonEmpty when it is not empty once trimmed of whitespace.

impl<T> NonEmpty for List<T>

A List is NonEmpty when it has at least one element.

module vault

The current vault: the source a program runs against. A host with a vault binds it as vault in the program module; a program running without one has no vault binding, and no module sees it.

The order is the walk's, never // the filesystem's, so `take(5)` answers the same on every machine. cards : Seq<Card> }
